original_obligation_source.truth_boundary: Targets and dependencies are carried from the authority register; historical machine-state prose is not revalidated live by this review.

open_obligations.title: Production WORLDLINE is still 1.7.3, so the promotion defects fixed in 1.8.0-1.9.1 are still authorized there
open_obligations.target: Production refuses every reproduced promotion defect: A (failed-check return), B (leftover synthetic world), C (undeclared empty roster), D (failed agent) and the typed-absence scenarios.
dependsOn: the operator's yes and password (or the install-authority actuator, G2/C7)

open_obligations.title: A later FAIL does not supersede an earlier PASS (one effective evaluation, SECURITY.md limit 8)
open_obligations.target: Each world has exactly one effective evaluation: the newest completed evaluation under the current requirement, PASS or FAIL, selected by the proved kernel. A newer evaluation supersedes every older one, and a superseded evaluation never regains authority (roadmap Phase 1 item 5).

open_obligations.title: A candidate can change the requirement that judges it and every later candidate (policy, verifier scope, protected set, examiners)
open_obligations.target: A candidate can never change the requirement that judges it or any later candidate: policy, verifier scope, protected set and examiners. The proved kernel refuses any such change (including a rewritten authoritative verifier, VERIFIER_MODIFIED_BY_CANDIDATE) in every promotion mode.

open_obligations.title: Candidate code can choose the verdict of a shared-process examiner (legacy one-identity checks; A5 strict variant declined)
open_obligations.target: A verdict that can authorize promotion comes from an examiner candidate code cannot reach or steer: determinate supervision (SUPERVISED, not stopped) and no candidate code in the examiner's process or identity (os._exit(0), unittest.SkipTest, monkeypatching can never yield an admitted PASS).

open_obligations.title: Checks whose verifier is unbound or only partly bound are admitted with a warning (make test, -m pytest, sh -c, undeclared helpers, covered script operands)
open_obligations.target: Every check that can authorize promotion binds a verifier identity staged from PRIME covering everything it executes or imports, including the process that actually decides the verdict (argv program and interpreter script operand), or the policy is refused at load.

open_obligations.title: For legacy checks, bytes the checks wrote are promoted as 'tested'
open_obligations.target: The promoted bytes are exactly the bytes examined before any check ran, immutable for the whole evaluation. Nothing a check, or candidate code it ran, wrote during checking can become PRIME.

open_obligations.title: Report verdicts are parsed permissively and decided by TESTED Python (skipped, failing or regressed runs read as PASS)
open_obligations.target: A report verdict is PASS only if at least one testcase executed and none failed, errored or was skipped, and a benchmark regression is FAIL. The verdict is computed in SPARK from facts produced independently of Python (Report_Facts).

open_obligations.title: Examiner imports are not confined to the staged bundle (PASS with unsatisfied imports admitted; candidate modules can run inside the private examiner)
open_obligations.target: No code from the candidate tree ever executes inside the examiner principal, and a PASS counts only when every import and read resolved inside the staged verifier bundle or the standard library; otherwise the check is EVALUATOR_INCOMPLETE. The evidence identifies every trusted input that influenced the verdict.

open_obligations.title: An admitted private report can carry a verdict the candidate wrote
open_obligations.target: An admitted report's verdict cannot be supplied by the candidate; a report that carries bytes the candidate wrote is not admissible.

open_obligations.title: candidate.run still starts candidate bytes under the worker's identity and broker
open_obligations.target: Candidate bytes never run under the worker principal; every candidate process runs as the candidate principal.

open_obligations.title: Private-evaluator roles can create nested user namespaces, and the cgroup-escape claim is not extended to them
open_obligations.target: Examiner, worker and candidate have nested user-namespace creation disabled, as worlds and checks do (--disable-userns), and a private role provably cannot leave its cgroup budget.

open_obligations.title: Case copies and the frozen-tree copy are not atomic snapshots
open_obligations.target: A case copy or frozen copy equals one consistent state of its source, even under a deliberate racing writer.

open_obligations.title: Private-report boundary facts are bootstrap literals and self-reports, not observations
open_obligations.target: Report boundary facts (mount exclusivity, role identity) are observed independently of the bootstrap before a report is admitted.

open_obligations.title: Legacy checks share one scratch overlay, so earlier checks can steer later examiners
open_obligations.target: Each required verdict depends only on the pre-check snapshot and its PRIME examiner.

open_obligations.title: Declared services run candidate code as the daemon account and could write live PRIME (A21)
open_obligations.target: Only the policy authority changes live PRIME; no candidate code can.

open_obligations.title: Declared services can make the supersession placeholder write fail, so an older PASS keeps speaking
open_obligations.target: The candidate has no veto over supersession (M3 soundness-1).

open_obligations.title: A candidate can plant a dormant judge in a non-primary root that takes over at the next primary switch (claim narrowed in M3 Decision 11)
open_obligations.target: The v2 claim: a candidate cannot plant a judge that takes over at the next primary switch. Neither a non-primary .worldline.json nor any examiner it names can be changed by a candidate and later adopted.

open_obligations.title: Symlinks, skipped directories (_WALK_SKIP) and file modes inside verifier scopes are outside the requirement (claim narrowed)
open_obligations.target: The v1 claim: the requirement covers every file in a verifier scope, so any candidate change an examiner could observe there is REQUIREMENT_CHANGED.

open_obligations.title: Staged bytes that differ from the candidate are published as a returnable checkpoint with no evaluation
open_obligations.target: Staged bytes that differ from the candidate are refused; they are never published as a PRIME checkpoint that can later be returned to.

open_obligations.title: An agent PASS ignores an OOM-killed subprocess
open_obligations.target: An agent whose subprocess was OOM-killed, or that hit a resource ceiling, is never PASS.

open_obligations.title: Production policy (janus) does not protect aegis-anubis verify/ or afterimage tools/
open_obligations.target: In production every examiner that a registered root's policy names is protected against candidate writes.

open_obligations.title: Re-running revalidation until a flaky check passes still authorizes (FAIL not terminal; anyone listed may request revalidation)
open_obligations.target: A FAIL under a requirement is terminal for that (world, requirement), and requesting an evaluation is a controlled capability, so re-running a flaky or host-dependent check cannot produce an authorizing PASS.

open_obligations.title: Every listed client holds full promotion and destruction authority, and nothing in the evidence records who asked
open_obligations.target: Collapse, return, transaction commit, abort, prune, revalidation requests, simulate and ghost enable are per-requester capabilities decided daemon-side (and for promotion, by the kernel). A commit's follow-on effects (starting PRIME's declared services, opening terminals and moving windows on the daemon account's desktop after a return) belong to the requester's capability, not free side effects, and a delegated socket fd confers nothing beyond its grant. Every receipt and causal event records the requester, hashed into the chain.

open_obligations.title: A checkpoint return can restore an older, looser policy (exempt from the requirement pair)
open_obligations.target: No listed-client act changes the judge in force; restoring an older policy needs an owner capability that binds the requirement it adopts.

open_obligations.title: Newest-speaks does not survive a rollback: a superseded pre-upgrade PASS revives
open_obligations.target: A superseded evaluation never regains authority, including across an engine rollback.

open_obligations.title: A checkpoint return checks that a world was once live, not that the restored bytes are that world's
open_obligations.target: A checkpoint return restores exactly the bytes checkpoint S had when displaced (S.components and content_id), witnessed by S's own committed receipt, and the kernel decides this.

open_obligations.title: Re-application under finalization-only evidence is not bound to the bytes re-applied
open_obligations.target: Re-application re-applies only W's evaluated bytes: W's delta_hash and components are verified against the re-applied payload and manifests.

open_obligations.title: Promotion mode, checkpoint witness and row resolution are decided by unproved Python over store fields and an ambiguous lookup
open_obligations.target: The promotion mode is derived from authenticated facts (the prepared transaction's typed mode), whether a return subject was ever live PRIME is decided by the proved Worldline.Ancestry over chained lineage records, and no alias can collide with an instance_id or content_id.

open_obligations.title: Prepare-to-commit change checks for the candidate payload are Python-only
open_obligations.target: Commit authorizes only if PRIME, the candidate payload and the record schema are what prepare saw, decided in the kernel.

open_obligations.title: Pair producer independence is assumed: one value passed to both sides of an identity pair satisfies the proof
open_obligations.target: Every identity pair Decide compares is produced from two independent records, and a value copied to both sides (or a wrong digest stated on both) cannot reach AUTHORIZED; Resulting_Requirement is never computed from live PRIME.

open_obligations.title: The evaluation admission path from raw observations to Admissible is not proved end to end (unproved C decode, Python classification carry, Boolean roster)
open_obligations.target: Promotion admissibility is decided in SPARK from raw observations: every decode/validate step on the authorization path is proved (as Collapse_Wire.Decode is), and Decide recomputes roster completeness itself.

open_obligations.title: A stored report status is never re-derived from the retained report bytes (dropped from M3 A3)
open_obligations.target: The status that speaks at promotion is re-derived from the retained report bytes by proved or independently produced code, so a store rewrite of the status is refused.

open_obligations.title: 'An ERROR head never authorizes' rests on a Python-written, unkeyed 'source' field (M3 Decision 15)
open_obligations.target: It is proved that an evaluation that did not complete never satisfies Roster_Complete.

open_obligations.title: Revalidation reads PRIME three times without a generation guard and trusts a stored base manifest
open_obligations.target: A revalidation context states exactly the requirement and verifier bytes its checks ran under, from one generation-guarded read, and stored base manifests are verified with verify_content.

open_obligations.title: The judge's execution identity (interpreter, tool and toolchain binaries, forwarded environment) is recorded by path only
open_obligations.target: Evidence is a statement about particular bytes under particular rules, including the interpreter, argv0 binaries and their libraries, sandbox and toolchain binaries and the forwarded environment; any change to them makes evidence stale.

open_obligations.title: Commit recomputes Resulting_Requirement from a staging location taken from the prepared record
open_obligations.target: Commit recomputes Resulting_Requirement from a location derived from the transaction id, never from JSON.

open_obligations.title: Ownership (uid/gid) is not recorded, so chown/chgrp in live PRIME is neither measured nor part of content identity
open_obligations.target: Every change to live PRIME that no record accounts for is measured, ownership included, and content identity covers ownership; a receipt never states foreignWorldContamination NONE while an unmeasured change is present.

open_obligations.title: Content roots and payload integrity omit behaviour-relevant metadata (modes, xattrs, ACLs, hard-link grouping, root-directory metadata, repository facts)
open_obligations.target: Two trees with the same content root behave the same, and payload integrity covers every field that can change behaviour; any exclusion is proven behaviour-neutral and stated in the kernel-facing spec.

open_obligations.title: Nothing checks at decision time that the kernel answering Decide is the proved build (library selectable by environment)
open_obligations.target: Every Decide is answered by the exact proved kernel build named in a root-owned, signed proof manifest; a substituted library can neither authorize a promotion nor obtain a PROVED receipt.

open_obligations.title: Kernel inputs read from the store and the prepared JSON are unauthenticated (same-uid forgery satisfies every pair)
open_obligations.target: Commit and recovery decide only on facts they recompute or on prepare-time facts, evaluation records, contexts, executed-verifier sets, history entries and epochs authenticated with a key a same-uid process cannot use; consistent forgery is detected and refused.

open_obligations.title: What is hashed and compared (manifests, canonical encoding, requirement/execution identities, report and resource admission, sandbox setup) is unproved Python
open_obligations.target: The values that reach the kernel are computed by proved code, or by an independent producer, from raw records: canonical encoding is injective and manifests, content roots and requirement identities are complete.

open_obligations.title: The staged tree can change between its commit-time recapture and the exchange
open_obligations.target: The bytes exchanged into PRIME are exactly the bytes the kernel authorized and the receipt's afterRoot and PRIME row name.

open_obligations.title: Reconcile and root removal change PRIME without a kernel decision
open_obligations.target: Whitepaper principle 1: nothing becomes real except through an authorized collapse; every PRIME generation change is a kernel-checked transition.

open_obligations.title: root.remove of the primary silently promotes remaining[0]
open_obligations.target: Every primary succession is explicit and receipted: root.remove of the primary refuses unless the successor is named, and the switch records the requirement it adopts.

open_obligations.title: No judge-change record and no mechanised, owner-authorized policy-change path (M3 Decision 6)
open_obligations.target: Every change to the requirement in force produces one ordered, receipted judge-change record (requirement before and after) through a mechanised owner-authorized path: live PRIME write, reconcile, restart resetting dirty, root.add/root.remove, engine or configuration change, checkpoint return.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 enforcement exists only as installed labs; production promotions are not governed by it, and protected heads have no production owner
open_obligations.target: Production promotions pass through the composed Authority v1 transaction (intent gate, capability issuer with consumed use, live examiner evidence chain, resource ledger, Universe registry), and the capability, evidence and Universe protected heads are composed and owned by the production authority. Mediation is enforced by the OS, not by convention: the daemon account's Python cannot mutate live PRIME except through the protected actuator, every actuation is re-observed and bound to durable transaction evidence, and a bypass campaign on the production topology shows it (roadmap Phase 2 exit gate).

open_obligations.title: Supervision facts come from journal scraping: a same-uid _COMM=systemd injection can forge SUPERVISED
open_obligations.target: Supervision facts (SUPERVISED, STOPPED, exit) come from an authenticated manager source that a same-uid process cannot forge and that does not depend on journal persistence.

open_obligations.title: The remaining C entry glue (pointer dereference, exception handlers, file/byte hashing marshalling) is pinned by digest, not proved
open_obligations.target: The unproved C surface is minimal (null check, call, exception-to-255 mapping) and every data-handling path, including hashing marshalling, is proved.

open_obligations.title: Recovery publishes PRIME without a kernel decision (unauthenticated markers; live capture for pre-1.9.0 records)
open_obligations.target: Every PRIME publication, including one completed by crash recovery, is authorized by a kernel decision recovery re-derives; recovery marks COMMITTED only after verifying that live/<key> resolves to the authorized staged payload and a durable one-shot authorization exists, otherwise it aborts or quarantines; an offline write is never folded into a collapse generation.

open_obligations.title: Deleting or rewriting config.json silently resets policy to fail-open defaults
open_obligations.target: A missing or altered config never lowers protection: network, resource ceilings and anchor export default closed; the config is integrity-bound; operator edits are never overwritten.

open_obligations.title: Admission fails open when its ledger is deleted and misses work outside the gate
open_obligations.target: Admission is decided by a proved rule and fails closed: it refuses when its ledger is missing, observes under its lock, meters all work including checks, doctor --refresh and git inspection, and its reservations satisfy the proved invariants of OB-198 (conservation, parent/child containment, no double release, no running workload without an active reservation), with the resource epoch an input to Decide (roadmap-requirements.md:105, :108).

open_obligations.title: The client-mode boundary depends on unit, install and account integrity the daemon does not verify
open_obligations.target: The daemon refuses to serve clients when its unit, drop-ins, install tree or account are writable by a client.

open_obligations.title: Disjointness of the client group and the daemon's group is only partly verified
open_obligations.target: No account is in both the client group and the daemon's group.

open_obligations.title: The client-mode gate can stay open with no checking daemon, and store-lock ambiguity leaves it as it was
open_obligations.target: The data-directory gate is open only while a daemon that checked the content is running; any ambiguity (hard-linked lock, cannot tell, relative XDG path) closes it.

open_obligations.title: The single-writer store lock can be defeated, and the store is opened and migrated before ownership checks
open_obligations.target: At most one daemon ever serves a store, and store ownership, type and schema are checked before any write.

open_obligations.title: Isolation binaries other than bubblewrap are not digest-pinned or attested
open_obligations.target: Every binary the private boundary relies on is digest-pinned in the run plan and re-checked before use.

open_obligations.title: Subordinate IDs mapped to the worker and candidate roles are not checked for use by other host accounts
open_obligations.target: The host identities mapped to worker and candidate belong to no other account on the host.

open_obligations.title: Sandbox construction and isolation are Python-configured and never checked against a declared specification
open_obligations.target: The isolation boundary (what a world, check, examiner or worker can see and write) is checked against a declared specification on every build.

open_obligations.title: SHA-256 functional correctness is tested against vectors, not proved
open_obligations.target: Every digest equality Decide proves rests on a hash implementation proved to compute SHA-256 (functional postconditions, not only absence of runtime errors).

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 C12: a root caller with a fresh operation id can drive the broker directly
open_obligations.target: The broker commits only promotions admitted by the intent gate and bound to the gate-journaled operation and capability, whatever the caller's uid.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 R1/C2: a promote can commit under a revoked grant
open_obligations.target: No promotion commits under a revoked grant; the broker rechecks the capability under its own lock before commit, and a queued recover cannot resume a promote the operator stopped.

open_obligations.title: Capability ID uniqueness is a value-only predicate over caller-supplied ancestry
open_obligations.target: Capability ID uniqueness is enforced against the custody registry, with the C ABI, adapter and replay inside the proof boundary.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 protected commit veto does not authenticate all daemon facts
open_obligations.target: Every daemon fact the root broker relies on is authenticated or independently re-derived, and evidence covers each fact.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 C5: the evidence policy pins neither the gate config nor the Genesis
open_obligations.target: The evidence binding pins the gate config and the Universe Genesis, so evidence cannot be replayed under another gate or Universe.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 F9: pre-existing absence-as-data sites remain
open_obligations.target: Nowhere in the authority stack does missing equal missing, or read as zero, empty or pass.

open_obligations.title: Audit finding 5: full protected Create_Child authority is open
open_obligations.target: Protected child admission is fully authorized (Create_Child authority).

open_obligations.title: Audit finding 7: the Genesis roster is not bound to its policy
open_obligations.target: The Genesis roster is bound to its policy.

open_obligations.title: COSMOGONY SPARK Quiet counters are vacuous and Can_Advance_Prime lacks exact succession
open_obligations.target: Quiet(U) is fed the observed counts of running worlds, reservations and unresolved transactions as Optional values, and Can_Advance_Prime requires Generation = Prime_Generation + 1.

open_obligations.title: Audit finding 6: hierarchy conservation is unproved
open_obligations.target: Hierarchy conservation is proved in SPARK.

open_obligations.title: Authority v1 E3: issuer reconcile does not re-chain from the anchored head
open_obligations.target: Issuer reconciliation verifies the event chain from the anchored head before accepting any state.

open_obligations.title: The managed inherited daemon lease is a cooperative singleton
open_obligations.target: The daemon singleton lease holds against a hostile same-UID process.

open_obligations.title: The operator-account boundary after the sudo cutover is not established (unrotated password, docker still in running processes, a NOPASSWD helper, no bypass campaign)
open_obligations.target: No agent and no process of the operator account can obtain root or write production state outside the protected path: sudo requires a password no agent has seen, docker (root-equivalent) membership is gone from every running process, the only NOPASSWD rule left is a reviewed read-only helper, and a bypass campaign run from the operator account itself (no sudo, no docker) against the installed production boundary shows it (operator directive section 1).

open_obligations.title: Release order enforcement depends on admin-changeable rulesets and on the tagged commit's own workflow
open_obligations.target: No version can be installed without an accepted assurance of the exact tagged commit, whatever the repository settings or workflow edits.

open_obligations.title: abort can delete the live PRIME payload
open_obligations.target: Abort never deletes a payload live PRIME resolves to and never acts on a quarantined transaction.

open_obligations.title: prune lets any listed client delete other clients' history and older checkpoint-return targets
open_obligations.target: Prune deletes only the requester's own history, never another client's worlds or lineage return targets without an owner capability, and walks paths race-free.

open_obligations.title: Commit durability is not guaranteed (best-effort directory fsync; COMMIT_DURABILITY_UNCERTAIN)
open_obligations.target: An exchange that happened is always recorded COMMITTED, durably and with its receipt, across any crash, and PRIME is never a torn tree.

open_obligations.title: The dirty flag is erased on every restart, and fork freeze never measures live against the PRIME row
open_obligations.target: No unrecorded PRIME write is frozen into a fork under a stale parent: dirty state survives restart and freeze measures live against the PRIME row.

open_obligations.title: Writes around the exchange are lost or attributed to the collapse (last generation read to renameat2; displaced tree; owned-window draining)
open_obligations.target: No write into live PRIME that WORLDLINE did not make is lost or published under a collapse receipt: every such write is refused before the exchange or recorded as an unaccounted-write with its bytes preserved.

open_obligations.title: root remove misses a write that lands between its re-read and the swap
open_obligations.target: root remove either carries every write to the operator's path or refuses.

open_obligations.title: PRIME write observation is incomplete (transient writes, mmap, external hard links) and freeze/reconcile ignore coverage
open_obligations.target: Every write into live PRIME not made by WORLDLINE is observed and accounted (as a generation or a foreign write) even if reverted, including mmap writes and writes through external hard links, and freeze and reconcile consult coverage.

open_obligations.title: worldline-relocate does not prove the copy complete
open_obligations.target: Relocation proves every retained payload and generation in the copy equals its recorded content identity.

open_obligations.title: Relocation trusts a caller's attestation that payloads were absent in the old store
open_obligations.target: A payload absence is exempted only on evidence the tool can verify.

open_obligations.title: The anchor export overwrites the only rollback evidence on every start and commit
open_obligations.target: A rolled-back local ledger is detected against a history-keeping external witness before any export, and export failures are reported.

open_obligations.title: Receipt 'invariantPreservation: PROVED' is issued on weaker grounds than it states
open_obligations.target: PROVED in a receipt means the running library is the product of a zero-exception proof, at or above the floor with pinned contracts, run for this library, and a skipped proof or malformed manifest never yields PROVED.

open_obligations.title: The proof gate does not pin every authority contract and parses GNATprove output by regex without checking summarySha256
open_obligations.target: The proof gate pins every contract authority depends on (receipts, causal_graph, world, ancestry as well as collapse, wire, identities, evaluation, transitions) and parses GNATprove output fail-closed with summarySha256 checked.

open_obligations.title: The store and its evidence are not tamper-evident against a same-uid process; the anchor key lives beside the store
open_obligations.target: Receipts, the causal chain and stored validation contexts are tamper-evident against any process except the daemon's own authority.

open_obligations.title: The external anchor (anchor.exportPath) is unset by default
open_obligations.target: An anchor copy the attacker cannot write always exists, so a store rewrite is always detectable.

open_obligations.title: The causal chain is not anchored; only committed receipts are
open_obligations.target: Causal events are appended to the signed, exported anchor too.

open_obligations.title: The anchor signs unverified store content, checks coverage by count and does not pin its key
open_obligations.target: The anchor signs only receipts it has verified, checks coverage by receipt identity, and pins its public key.

open_obligations.title: The receipt chain leaves transaction ids and its head unverified; the chain genesis witness was deferred to M3 and dropped
open_obligations.target: The receipt chain binds transaction ids and has an externally witnessed genesis and head, so tail deletion and re-pointing are detected, and receipts are issued only from authenticated records. Chain acceptance and verification go through the exported, proved Worldline.Receipts.Append and Causal_Graph.Append (OB-197), never a Python comparison (roadmap Phase 1 item 6).

open_obligations.title: Agent-authored causal events are chained and reported as if WORLDLINE wrote them
open_obligations.target: Only WORLDLINE can author events with reserved actors or kinds, and why separates agent claims from WORLDLINE facts.

open_obligations.title: The CLI accepts a same-uid impostor as the daemon
